home.challengeDesc: Race against the clock and push your speed
home.allDone: All levels complete! Review the chapters

chapters.subtitle: Pick a chapter to begin your tmux journey

1-1.title: Meet tmux
1-1.description: Create a tmux session and attach to it

1-2.title: Split Operations
1-2.description: Make one side-by-side split and one stacked split, ending with at least 3 panes

1-3.title: Pane Navigation
1-3.description: Move from the top-left pane to the bottom-right pane marked '>>> TARGET <<<', keeping all four panes

1-4.title: Close Pane
1-4.description: Close the top-right pane marked 'CLOSE ME' and keep the other two panes

1-5.title: Four Grid Layout
1-5.description: Turn one pane into a 2×2 grid of four equal panes

1-6.title: Pane Zoom
1-6.description: Zoom the pane showing 'SECRET DATA' to fill the window, keeping all three panes

1-7.title: New Window
1-7.description: Have exactly 3 windows in this session

1-8.title: Window Switching
1-8.description: Switch to the third window, 'gamma', keeping all three windows

1-9.title: Window Naming
1-9.description: Rename the three windows, in order, to 'editor', 'server' and 'logs'

1-10.title: Detach & Attach
1-10.description: Detach from session 'mywork', then attach to it again

1-11.title: Final Exam
1-11.description: Build three windows in order: 'editor' (two panes side by side), 'server' (one pane), 'logs' (two panes stacked)

2-1.title: Resize Panes
2-1.description: Widen the left pane to about 70% of the window width (between 67% and 73%)

2-2.title: Preset Layouts
2-2.description: Use the even-horizontal preset to put the three panes in one row of equal width

2-3.title: Swap Panes
2-3.description: Swap the two panes so Panel A is on the left and Panel B on the right

2-4.title: Pane-Window Conversion
2-4.description: Break the server log pane out of 'main' into its own window, then join the notes pane from window 'temp' into 'main', side by side with editor

2-5.title: Copy Mode
2-5.description: Use copy mode to copy the line 'Alpha-Bravo-Charlie' in the left pane, then paste it into the right pane

2-6.title: Synchronized Panes
2-6.description: Turn on pane synchronization in window 'servers', then type echo deploy so all three panes run it at once

2-7.title: Session Management
2-7.description: From session 'default', create sessions 'dev' and 'staging' in the background, then switch to 'dev'

2-8.title: Final Exam
2-8.description: Build a debug environment: session 'debug' with window 'services' (three equal, side-by-side, synchronized panes) and window 'db', and end up in 'debug'

3-1.title: Key Customization
3-1.description: Change the prefix to Ctrl+a, bind | to a side-by-side split, then split once with Ctrl+a |

3-2.title: Mouse Mode
3-2.description: Turn mouse mode on and click the right pane p2

3-3.title: Status Bar
3-3.description: Make the status bar background blue (bg=blue) and show the time (%H:%M) on the right

3-4.title: Config File
3-4.description: Write ~/.tmux.conf in the editor (prefix C-a, mouse on, r reloads the config), load it, then reload it with Ctrl+a r

3-5.title: Scripted Setup
3-5.description: Write ~/dev.sh and run it with bash: session 'dev', window 'editor' with two panes side by side, window 'server' running npm run dev, then attach to 'dev'

3-6.title: Advanced Windows
3-6.description: Use move-window to move the window 'tools' from session 'utils' to session 'project'

3-7.title: Final Exam
3-7.description: Write the config ~/.tmux.conf and the start script ~/work.sh, run the script to enter session 'work', then split window 'main' side by side with Ctrl+a |

objectives.1-2-side-by-side: Split once side by side with `Ctrl+b %`
objectives.1-2-stacked: Split once top and bottom with `Ctrl+b "`
objectives.1-2-three-panes: The window has at least 3 panes, some side by side and some stacked
objectives.1-9-editor: The first window (number 0) is renamed to 'editor'
objectives.1-9-server: The second window (number 1) is renamed to 'server'
objectives.1-9-logs: The third window (number 2) is renamed to 'logs', with no extra windows
objectives.1-10-reattach: After detaching, attach to 'mywork' again with `tmux attach -t mywork`
objectives.1-11-editor: The first window is named 'editor' and has two panes side by side
objectives.1-11-server: The second window is named 'server' and has one pane
objectives.1-11-logs: The third and last window is named 'logs' and has two panes stacked
objectives.2-1-resize: The left pane takes 67% to 73% of the window width, and the two panes are still side by side
objectives.2-2-even: The original three panes sit side by side in one row, each a third of the width
objectives.2-3-swap: The Panel A pane is on the left and the Panel B pane on the right (move the panes themselves; changing their text does not count)
objectives.2-4-break: The server log pane is alone in a new window (broken out with `Ctrl+b !`)
objectives.2-4-join: The notes pane is joined into 'main' with `join-pane`, side by side with editor; the 'temp' window goes away
objectives.2-5-copy: In copy mode, select and copy exactly the line 'Alpha-Bravo-Charlie', nothing more or less
objectives.2-5-paste: Paste the copied line into the right pane with `Ctrl+b ]`
objectives.2-6-sync: synchronize-panes is on in window 'servers', and still on at the end
objectives.2-6-broadcast: With sync on, type `echo deploy` so that it runs in all three panes at once
objectives.2-7-sessions: Sessions 'default', 'dev' and 'staging' all exist, and 'default' is still the session you started in (do not rename it)
objectives.2-8-session: Create a new session 'debug' and be attached to it (renaming the session you started in does not count)
objectives.2-8-panes: Window 'services' in 'debug' has three panes side by side, of equal width
objectives.3-1-bind: `|` is bound in the prefix table to a side-by-side split, `split-window -h`
objectives.3-1-split: With the new prefix, press `Ctrl+a |` to split side by side once
objectives.3-2-click: Click the right pane p2 with the mouse so it becomes the active pane
objectives.3-4-saved: Write and save `~/.tmux.conf` in the editor
objectives.3-4-loaded: Load `~/.tmux.conf` with `source-file`; lines of this file set the prefix to `C-a`, turn `mouse` on and bind `r` to `source-file ~/.tmux.conf`
objectives.3-4-reloaded: Press `Ctrl+a r` to reload the config
objectives.3-5-editor: The script created window 'editor' in 'dev' and split it into 2 panes side by side
objectives.3-5-server: The script created window 'server' in 'dev' and ran `npm run dev` in it with `send-keys`
objectives.3-5-attached: You end up attached to session 'dev'
objectives.3-7-config: Lines of `~/.tmux.conf` set the prefix to `C-a` and bind `|` to `split-window -h`
objectives.3-7-session: A script created session 'work' (with window 'main') and you are attached to it
objectives.3-7-split: With `C-a` as the prefix, press `Ctrl+a |` to split window 'main' into 2 panes side by side

hints.1-1-1: A session is where tmux keeps your work. Typing `tmux` creates one and puts you in it.
hints.1-1-2: `tmux new -s <name>` creates a session with a name you choose.
hints.1-2-1: You need one split of each kind: one that puts panes side by side and one that stacks them.
hints.1-2-2: `Ctrl+b %` splits the active pane into left and right; `Ctrl+b "` splits it into top and bottom.
hints.1-3-1: Press `Ctrl+b` and then an arrow key to move to the pane in that direction.
hints.1-3-2: You are in the top-left pane and the target is bottom right: one step right, one step down.
hints.1-4-1: `Ctrl+b x` closes the active pane (tmux asks first; press `y` to confirm). At the start the active pane is the left one, not the one to close.
hints.1-4-2: Move to the 'CLOSE ME' pane with `Ctrl+b →` first, then press `Ctrl+b x` and answer `y` when tmux asks at the bottom (or type `exit` in it).
hints.1-4-3: Press `Ctrl+b →`, then `Ctrl+b x`, then `y` to confirm
hints.1-5-1: Every split cuts the active pane in half. Split once, then split each half.
hints.1-5-2: `Ctrl+b %` splits left and right, `Ctrl+b "` splits top and bottom. After a split the new pane has focus; `Ctrl+b ←` takes you back to the left half.
hints.1-6-1: `Ctrl+b z` zooms the active pane to fill the window; press it again to restore.
hints.1-6-2: 'SECRET DATA' is in the top-right pane. Move there with `Ctrl+b →` first, then zoom.
hints.1-7-2: You have 1 window; create 2 more. The total must be exactly 3, no more.
hints.1-8-1: `Ctrl+b n` goes to the next window, `Ctrl+b p` to the previous one.
hints.1-8-2: `Ctrl+b` followed by a number goes straight to that window. Numbers start at 0.
hints.1-9-1: `Ctrl+b ,` renames the current window: delete the old name, type the new one and press Enter.
hints.1-9-2: Rename window 0, then go to the next window with `Ctrl+b n` and rename that one.
hints.1-10-1: A detached session keeps running in the background, and you can attach to it again later.
hints.1-10-2: `Ctrl+b d` detaches. `tmux attach -t <name>` attaches to a session by name.
hints.1-10-3: Press `Ctrl+b d`, then type `tmux attach -t mywork`
hints.1-11-1: First rename the current window to editor and split it side by side, then add the other two windows.
hints.1-11-2: `:new-window -n server` creates and names a window in one step. `Ctrl+b %` splits side by side, `Ctrl+b "` stacks.
hints.2-1-1: The left pane is the active one. Resizing it moves its right border: move the border right and the left pane gets wider.
hints.2-1-2: `Ctrl+b Alt+→` moves the border right by 5% of the width, `Ctrl+b Ctrl+→` by 1%. Press the prefix before each one.
hints.2-2-1: tmux has preset layouts that rearrange every pane in a window with one command.
hints.2-2-2: `Ctrl+b Space` steps through the presets; in this window the first press gives even-horizontal. `:select-layout` with a layout name picks one directly.
hints.2-3-1: No need to rebuild anything: tmux can swap two panes in place.
hints.2-3-2: `Ctrl+b }` swaps the active pane with the next one, `Ctrl+b {` with the previous one. With two panes both do the same.
hints.2-4-1: `break-pane` turns a pane into a window of its own; `join-pane` brings a pane over from another window.
hints.2-4-2: The active pane is server log, so `Ctrl+b !` breaks it out. In `:join-pane -h -s from -t to`, `-s` is the pane to move, `-t` the pane to put it next to, and `-h` means side by side; a window name stands for that window's active pane.
hints.2-5-1: tmux has its own copy and paste: select and copy text in copy mode, then paste it in another pane. Typing the code yourself does not count.
hints.2-5-2: `Ctrl+b [` enters copy mode with the cursor at the start of the last line. `Space` starts a selection, `$` jumps to the end of the line, `Enter` copies and leaves copy mode. `Ctrl+b ]` pastes.
hints.2-5-3: Press `Ctrl+b [`, `Space`, `$`, `Enter`, then `Ctrl+b →` to go to the right pane, then `Ctrl+b ]`
hints.2-6-1: With panes synchronized, every line you type goes to all panes of the window at once.
hints.2-6-2: Turn it on with `:setw synchronize-panes on` (`off` turns it off). Typing into each pane one by one without sync does not count.
hints.2-7-1: You are already inside tmux. Typing `tmux new -s dev` at the shell fails, because tmux will not nest sessions. Adding `-d` creates the session in the background without attaching to it.
hints.2-7-2: Create both sessions with `tmux new -d -s name`, then move your client there with `tmux switch-client -t name`.
hints.2-7-3: Type `tmux new -d -s dev`, `tmux new -d -s staging`, then `tmux switch-client -t dev`
hints.2-8-1: Put the chapter together: create a session in the background and switch to it, split, apply a preset layout, turn on sync, add a window.
hints.2-8-2: `tmux new -d -s debug -n services` creates the session and names its first window services. `Ctrl+b %` splits side by side, `:select-layout even-horizontal` evens the widths, `:new-window -n db` adds a window. Turn sync on while you are in services.
hints.2-8-3: In order: `tmux new -d -s debug -n services`, `tmux switch-client -t debug`, `Ctrl+b %` twice, `:select-layout even-horizontal`, `:setw synchronize-panes on`, `:new-window -n db`
hints.3-1-1: Many people move the prefix from `Ctrl+b` to the handier `Ctrl+a` and give common actions an easy key. In a browser `Ctrl+a` normally selects all, but once it is the prefix the game takes it.
hints.3-1-2: `:set -g prefix C-a` changes the prefix, and `:bind-key | split-window -h` makes `|` after the prefix split side by side.
hints.3-1-3: Type `:set -g prefix C-a`, then `:bind-key | split-window -h`, then press `Ctrl+a |`
hints.3-2-1: With mouse mode on, clicking a pane switches to it. Switching with the keyboard does not count.
hints.3-2-2: `:set -g mouse on` turns mouse mode on. While it is off, clicking a pane does nothing.
hints.3-2-3: Type `:set -g mouse on`, then click the right pane p2
hints.3-3-1: `status-style` sets the status bar colours, and `status-right` sets what its right side shows.
hints.3-3-2: The colour is written `bg=blue`; in the time format `%H` is the hour and `%M` the minute.
hints.3-4-1: Settings in `~/.tmux.conf` do not have to be typed every time. A tmux server reads this file when it starts; one that is already running, like yours now, needs `source-file` to load it. Bind a key that reloads it, so changes take effect at once.
hints.3-4-2: `vim ~/.tmux.conf` opens the editor, and saving closes it. `:source-file ~/.tmux.conf` loads the file; the line `bind r source-file ~/.tmux.conf` makes `Ctrl+a r` reload it.
hints.3-4-3: Type `vim ~/.tmux.conf`, write three lines: `set -g prefix C-a`, `set -g mouse on`, `bind r source-file ~/.tmux.conf`, click Save; then type `:source-file ~/.tmux.conf` and press `Ctrl+a r`
hints.3-5-1: Put the tmux commands that build your workspace in a script and one command sets it all up. The script runs outside tmux, so create the session in the background with `-d` and name targets with `-t`.
hints.3-5-2: Write the script with `vim ~/dev.sh` and run it with `bash ~/dev.sh`. `tmux send-keys -t dev:server 'npm run dev' Enter` types a command into a window and presses Enter; `tmux attach -t dev` enters the session.
hints.3-5-3: Type `vim ~/dev.sh`, write five lines: `tmux new-session -d -s dev -n editor`, `tmux split-window -h -t dev:editor`, `tmux new-window -t dev -n server`, `tmux send-keys -t dev:server 'npm run dev' Enter`, `tmux attach -t dev`, click Save; then type `bash ~/dev.sh`
hints.3-6-1: A window can move to another session and stay the same window. Creating a new window with the same name does not count.
hints.3-6-2: `move-window` takes the window to move as `-s session:window` and the destination as `-t session:`. When the last window leaves 'utils', that session closes by itself.
hints.3-7-1: Put it all together: a config file changes the prefix and binds a key, a start script builds the session, and your own key splits it. No tmux server is running yet, and a server reads `~/.tmux.conf` when it starts, so write the config first and run the script after.
hints.3-7-2: The config has `set -g prefix C-a` and `bind | split-window -h`; the script runs `tmux new-session -d -s work -n main` and enters with `tmux attach -t work`. If you wrote the config after the server had started, load it with `:source-file ~/.tmux.conf`.
hints.3-7-3: Type `vim ~/.tmux.conf`, write two lines: `set -g prefix C-a`, `bind | split-window -h`, click Save; type `vim ~/work.sh`, write two lines: `tmux new-session -d -s work -n main`, `tmux attach -t work`, click Save; type `bash ~/work.sh`, then press `Ctrl+a |`

tutorial.1-2-step1: Press `Ctrl+b %` to split the pane into left and right
tutorial.1-2-step2: Press `Ctrl+b "` to split the active pane into top and bottom
tutorial.1-3-step1: Press `Ctrl+b →` to move to the right column
tutorial.1-3-step2: Press `Ctrl+b ↓` to move down to the target pane
tutorial.1-4-step1: Press `Ctrl+b →` to move to the 'CLOSE ME' pane
tutorial.1-5-step1: Press `Ctrl+b %` to split into left and right halves
tutorial.1-5-step2: Press `Ctrl+b "` to split the right half into top and bottom
tutorial.1-5-step3: Press `Ctrl+b ←` to go back to the left half, then `Ctrl+b "` to split it too
tutorial.1-6-step1: Press `Ctrl+b →` to move to the 'SECRET DATA' pane
tutorial.1-7-step1: Press `Ctrl+b c` to create the second window
tutorial.1-7-step2: Press `Ctrl+b c` again to create the third window
tutorial.1-9-step2: Press `Ctrl+b n` to go to window 1 and rename it to `server` with `Ctrl+b ,`
tutorial.1-9-step3: Press `Ctrl+b n` again to go to window 2 and rename it to `logs` with `Ctrl+b ,`
tutorial.1-10-step1: Press `Ctrl+b d` to detach from the session
tutorial.1-10-step2: Type `tmux attach -t mywork` to attach again
tutorial.1-11-step1: Press `Ctrl+b ,` and rename the current window to `editor`
tutorial.1-11-step2: Press `Ctrl+b %` to split editor into two panes side by side
tutorial.1-11-step3: Type `:new-window -n server` to create the server window
tutorial.1-11-step4: Type `:new-window -n logs` to create the logs window
tutorial.1-11-step5: Press `Ctrl+b "` to split logs into two stacked panes
tutorial.2-1-step1: Press `Ctrl+b Alt+→` once: the border moves right by 5% and the left pane is now 55% wide
tutorial.2-1-step2: Press `Ctrl+b Alt+→` 3 more times, until the left pane is about 70% wide
tutorial.2-4-step1: Press `Ctrl+b !` to break the active server log pane out into a new window
tutorial.2-4-step2: Type `:join-pane -h -s temp -t main` to move the notes pane next to editor in 'main'
tutorial.2-5-step1: In the left pane press `Ctrl+b [` to enter copy mode; the cursor sits at the start of the last line. If that is not the 'Alpha-Bravo-Charlie' line, press `↑` to move onto it
tutorial.2-5-step2: Press `Space` to start selecting, `$` to select to the end of the line, `Enter` to copy
tutorial.2-5-step3: Press `Ctrl+b →` to go to the right pane
tutorial.2-6-step1: Type `:setw synchronize-panes on` to turn sync on
tutorial.2-6-step2: Type `echo deploy`; it runs in all three panes at once
tutorial.2-7-step1: Type `tmux new -d -s dev` to create 'dev' in the background
tutorial.2-7-step2: Type `tmux new -d -s staging` to create 'staging' in the background
tutorial.2-7-step3: Type `tmux switch-client -t dev` to switch to 'dev'
tutorial.2-8-step1: Type `tmux new -d -s debug -n services` to create session 'debug' in the background, with first window 'services'
tutorial.2-8-step2: Type `tmux switch-client -t debug` to switch to 'debug'
tutorial.2-8-step3: Press `Ctrl+b %` twice to split 'services' into three panes
tutorial.2-8-step4: Type `:select-layout even-horizontal` to give the three panes equal width
tutorial.2-8-step5: Type `:setw synchronize-panes on` to turn on sync in 'services'
tutorial.3-1-step1: Type `:set -g prefix C-a` to make `Ctrl+a` the prefix
tutorial.3-1-step2: Type `:bind-key | split-window -h` to bind `|` to a side-by-side split
tutorial.3-1-step3: Press `Ctrl+a |` to split with your new key
tutorial.3-2-step1: Type `:set -g mouse on` to turn mouse mode on
tutorial.3-3-step1: Type `:set -g status-style bg=blue` to make the status bar blue
tutorial.3-3-step2: Type `:set -g status-right "%H:%M"` to show the time on the right
tutorial.3-4-step1: Type `vim ~/.tmux.conf`, write the three lines and click Save
tutorial.3-4-step3: Press `Ctrl+a r` to reload the config
tutorial.3-5-step1: Type `vim ~/dev.sh`, write the script and click Save
tutorial.3-7-step1: Type `vim ~/.tmux.conf`, write the config and click Save
tutorial.3-7-step2: Type `vim ~/work.sh`, write the script and click Save
tutorial.3-7-step3: Type `bash ~/work.sh`: the starting server reads `~/.tmux.conf`, and the script creates session 'work' and attaches
tutorial.3-7-step4: Press `Ctrl+a |` to split window 'main' side by side

challenge.title: Challenge Mode
challenge.beginnerDesc: Make 2–3 named windows, each with 1 pane, 2 side by side or 2 stacked (other windows don't count)
challenge.intermediateDesc: One at random: 3–4 equal panes in a row or column, a 2×2 grid plus a window, synchronized panes, or a zoomed pane
challenge.advancedDesc: Build two named sessions with named windows and layouts, then set one global option

tasks.windowSingle: The current session has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly 1 pane
tasks.windowRow: The current session has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly {{count}} panes side by side
tasks.windowColumn: The current session has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly {{count}} panes stacked top to bottom
tasks.windowEvenRow: The current session has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly {{count}} panes side by side, all the same width
tasks.windowEvenColumn: The current session has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly {{count}} panes stacked top to bottom, all the same height
tasks.windowGrid: The current session has a window named '{{window}}' laid out as a 2×2 grid: exactly 4 panes of the same size, two across and two down

tasks.windowZoomed: A pane of window '{{window}}' in the current session is zoomed
tasks.sessionWindowSingle: Session '{{session}}' has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly 1 pane
tasks.sessionWindowRow: Session '{{session}}' has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly {{count}} panes side by side
tasks.sessionWindowColumn: Session '{{session}}' has a window named '{{window}}' with exactly {{count}} panes stacked top to bottom

reference.title: Command Reference

descriptions.session: Create, attach, and manage tmux sessions
descriptions.window: Create and switch between windows in a session
descriptions.pane: Split, navigate, and resize pane layouts
descriptions.copy: Copy and paste text between panes

entries.new-session: Start a session named work and go into it (typed outside tmux)
entries.attach: Go back into the existing session work
entries.detach: Leave the session; it keeps running in the background
entries.new-detached: Create session dev in the background without switching to it
entries.switch-client: Switch to session dev from inside tmux
entries.rename-session: Rename the current session: type the new name and press `Enter`
entries.kill-session: Close session dev and every window in it
entries.new-window-named: Create a new window named logs
entries.select-window: Jump straight to a window by its number (here 1); any of `0` to `9` works
entries.rename-window: Rename the current window: type the new name and press `Enter`
entries.kill-window: Close the current window: tmux asks first, press `y` to confirm
entries.move-window: Move window tools from session utils into session project
entries.split-side: Split the active pane into left and right
entries.split-stacked: Split the active pane into top and bottom
entries.select-pane: Move to the pane in the direction of the arrow
entries.next-pane: Go to the next pane in turn
entries.kill-pane: Close the active pane: tmux asks first, press `y` to confirm
entries.zoom-pane: Zoom the active pane to fill the window; press again to restore it
entries.resize-pane: Resize the pane towards the arrow, 1 cell at a time
entries.resize-pane-5: Resize the pane towards the arrow, 5 cells at a time
entries.swap-pane: Swap the pane with the previous (`{`) or the next (`}`) one
entries.break-pane: Break the active pane out into a window of its own
entries.join-pane: Join the pane of window temp into window main, side by side
entries.select-layout: Put all panes side by side at equal widths; even-vertical, main-horizontal, main-vertical and tiled work too
entries.synchronize-panes: Type into every pane of the window at once; set it to off to stop
entries.copy-mode: Enter copy mode to move around the pane and select text
entries.copy-move: Move the cursor in copy mode (`h` `j` `k` `l` work too)
entries.copy-select: Start a selection at the cursor in copy mode
entries.copy-copy: Copy the selection and leave copy mode
entries.paste: Paste the last copied text into the active pane
entries.command-prompt: Open the tmux command prompt, type a command and press `Enter`; in the game you can also type a command starting with `:` in the command box
entries.bind-key: Add a binding: the prefix then `|` splits left and right
entries.mouse: Turn on the mouse: click a pane to select it, drag a border to resize

parse.ambiguousCommand: ambiguous command: {{command}}, could be: {{matches}}. Type more of the name.
parse.tooManyArgs: {{command}}: too many arguments (put text with spaces in quotes)
parse.unterminatedQuote: missing closing quote: every ' or " must be closed

command.unsupported: {{command}} is a real tmux command, but the simulator does not support it yet

state.detached: not attached to a session: run tmux attach first

target.sessionNotFound: can't find session: {{target}} (tmux ls lists sessions)

session.none: no server running: start one with tmux new
session.duplicate: duplicate session: {{name}}. Pick another name, or attach to it with tmux attach -t {{name}}
session.nested: sessions should be nested with care: you are already inside tmux. Add -d to create the session in the background, or detach first (tmux detach)
session.badName: bad session name: {{name}} (it must not be empty or contain : or .)
session.nestedAttach: sessions should be nested with care: you are already inside tmux. To go to another session, use tmux switch-client -t <name>

window.indexInUse: index in use: {{index}}. Choose a free window index

pane.onlyOne: can't break with only one pane: split the window first
pane.same: source and target panes must be different
pane.noSpace: no space for new pane: the pane is too small, make it bigger or close another pane first

layout.unknown: invalid layout: {{layout}} (try even-horizontal, even-vertical, main-horizontal, main-vertical or tiled)

option.unsupported: {{option}} is a real tmux option, but the simulator does not support it yet

key.reserved: {{key}} is taken by the browser and can't be used here; pick another key
key.unbound: no key bound to {{key}} after the prefix
key.tableUnsupported: key table {{table}} is not supported: use prefix or root

script.depth: {{path}}: too many nested files (a file keeps sourcing itself?)

shell.unsupported: the simulator's shell does not support {{token}} (pipes and redirects); put it in quotes to use it as text

buffer.empty: no buffers: copy some text first
